subject: Private Edge: Canary rollout & pinned-version maintenance window (proposal)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: ops@acmehealth.com, deploy@vendorcorp.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private Edge: Canary rollout & pinned-version maintenance window (proposal)

Hi team,

I want to propose a narrow maintenance window and a canary-first rollback choreography for the Private Edge clusters we operate for AcmeHealth. Goal: apply the security micro-patch (release v3.4.1) with pinned-serving binaries while preserving live request SLOs and a fast, automated rollback path.

Proposed window
- UTC: 2027-05-12 02:00 - 06:00 (US region preferred)
- Local engineering start: 2027-05-12 01:00 PDT (prep and canary validation)

High-level plan
- Preflight (48h): config diff, canary image build, metrics baseline capture.
- Canary (30 min): route 5% of traffic to a single canary node group; monitor latency, 4xx/5xx, KV cache hit, and memory.
- Ramp (30-90 min): 5 -> 25 -> 50% increments if canary metrics hold.
- Pin: update cluster pin file to v3.4.1 only after 50% stable for 30m.
- Sweep & finalize (remaining window): remaining servers drained and replaced.

Rollback triggers (automated + manual)
- Automated: 2x baseline 95p latency OR >1% sustained 5xx for 5 minutes OR KV cache miss rate >10% vs baseline.
- Manual: SRE or Acme on-call raises immediate rollback.

Rollback choreography (short summary)
1) Immediately stop routing to canary node group (API proxy config + routing policy).
2) Re-pin to previous stable image and trigger redeploy of canary group.
3) If >10% of nodes in rollout fail to drain or restart: circuit-break to cold standby (pre-warmed).

Network and path considerations (questions for Acme ops)
- Will you allow BGP route withdraws for canary nodes, or do we rely solely on API-proxy traffic splits?
- Any ACL/NGFW approval required for the rolling IPs?

Attachments: private-edge_patch_proposal_v1.pdf, canary-metrics-checklist.xlsx
Drive runbook link: https://drive.redwood.com/open?id=1A2B3C-canary-runbook

Action items
- Acme ops: confirm network ACL and BGP handling by EOD 2027-05-03.
- Vendor (VendorCorp): confirm your sidecar image compatibility with v3.4.1 and provide any required preflight hooks.
- Redwood: Karthik to share the KV-cache drain script and canary rollback playbook.

I suggest a 30-minute pre-window sync two days before the window to rehearse the rollback.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Acme Health Ops <ops@acmehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, deploy@vendorcorp.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 12:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Edge: Canary rollout & pinned-version maintenance window (proposal)

Irene,

Thanks for the detailed plan — overall looks good. A couple items we need clarified before we commit:

1) BGP vs proxy routing: Our environment prefers not to withdraw BGP announcements during maintenance; we avoid route churn because of multi-site peering. Can you confirm that API-proxy traffic-splitting alone is sufficient for canary isolation (we can gate IP-level controls if absolutely needed)?

2) Database connections: some on-prem DB connections are sticky to the pod IP. How do you plan to handle session affinity during canary? Will you terminate connections gracefully?

3) Rollback time budget: given our monitoring team needs to validate reports, can we extend the canary observation to 45 minutes at 5% before ramping if we see volatile metrics?

We will check ACLs and give formal feedback by 2027-05-03 as requested.

- Acme Ops (Sam R.)
SRE Lead, Acme Health Ops
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, ops@acmehealth.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, deploy@vendorcorp.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Edge: Canary rollout & pinned-version maintenance window (proposal)

Sam / team,

Short answers up front:
- API-proxy traffic-splitting is sufficient for request-level isolation. We will not require BGP withdraws.
- Session affinity: our runtime supports graceful connection draining. Plan: set session TTL to 30s, initiate a graceful drain during each node cordon, and run a connection drain check before decommission.
- Canary observation: +45m at 5% is OK. We'll include an extended hold state in the playbook.

Implementation notes (operational commands & checks)
- KV cache drain (run on canary node group):
  - /opt/redwood/bin/drain-kv --cluster private-edge-acme --group canary --wait 300
  - verify: curl -s http://localhost:9100/kv/hit-rate | jq .recent | compare-with-baseline
- Proxy routing toggle (API):
  - POST /admin/routing/split {"cluster":"private-edge-acme","split":{"canary":5,"primary":95}}
  - rollback: POST /admin/routing/split {"cluster":"private-edge-acme","split":{"canary":0,"primary":100}}
- Redeploy pinned image:
  - ansible-playbook -i hosts/private-edge canary-deploy.yml --extra-vars \"image_tag=v3.4.1 pin=true\"
- Health checks to gate each ramp step:
  - 95p latency (slo_latency_ms)
  - 5xx rate (cluster_5xx_rate)
  - kv_miss_ratio

Automated rollback hook (what will actually happen if trigger fires)
1) Routing API sets canary=0 (instant)
2) Ansible redeploys canary nodes with previous image_tag=v3.4.0 and restarts runtime processes in sequence (ordered by drain status)
3) Alert to on-call + open incident ticket with prefilled diagnostics pack (logs, metrics snapshot, recent traces)

I'll attach a small test playbook to the runbook for your infra team to review.

Karthik
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: ops@acmehealth.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, deploy@vendorcorp.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Edge: Canary rollout & pinned-version maintenance window (proposal)

Thanks for the quick answers and Karthik for the commands — that clarifies the execution path. Agreed next steps: 

- Acme Ops (Sam): confirm ACL/NGFW exceptions and session-affinity tolerances by 2027-05-03 EOD.
- VendorCorp: please validate sidecar compatibility with v3.4.1 and provide any preflight hooks by 2027-05-05.
- Redwood (Karthik): add the 45-minute extended hold state at 5% into the runbook and upload the playbook snippet to the Drive runbook.
- All: 30-minute dry run rehearsal on 2027-05-10 02:00 UTC (will send invite).

I will update the pinned document (private-edge_patch_proposal_v1.pdf) with these decisions and circulate the final runbook link once Karthik uploads the snippet.

If no objections by Monday EOD we will lock the 2027-05-12 window.

Best,
Irene
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
